chunks: My father narrated to him, may God be pleased with him, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ali ibn al-Salt narrated to me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fazal, from Asim ibn Hamid, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Abdullah ibn al-Hasan, from his mother Fatimah bint al-Husayn (peace be upon them both), from her father (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:

Three characteristics: whoever possesses them has perfected the characteristics of faith: The one who, when pleased, his pleasure does not lead him into sin or falsehood; and when angered, his anger does not lead him away from the truth; and when in power, he does not acquire what does not belong to him.

key_terms.قَدَرَ: was in power or had ability

ai.seo_question: What are the three characteristics that perfect faith according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, this hadith links emotional regulation to the perfection of *Iman*, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the interplay between inner character and outward action. The three traits—moderation in pleasure, justice in anger, and restraint in power—mirror the Prophetic ideal of *Hilm* (forbearance) and *Adl* (justice), serving as practical markers of spiritual maturity. This narration underscores that true faith is not merely belief but is manifested through consistent ethical conduct in varying emotional states.
